changes.before: Remove only the selected record by ID, preserving the old array and handling the last item.
changes.after: Remove one record by making a new array of the records you want to keep.

before: filter returns a new array containing the elements whose callback returns true. To remove one selected ID, keep records with a different ID. This changes membership without splicing the old state array. Existing kept objects are shared; filter does not deep-copy them.

without(tasks, id) accepts the old array and an ID, then returns the filtered array. task.id !== id means keep this record if its ID is not strictly equal to the target. Each remove callback captures its own task ID, not its label or position. setTasks uses pending state; map renders the remaining records with stable keys.

Optional practice: Call without with an absent ID and explain why all records remain. The checks cover these finite behaviors; a matching DOM alone does not prove every implementation choice. The frame supplies React and mounts App. No imports, server, persistence or network are involved.
after: `filter` makes a new array. Its test decides which items to keep. To remove a chosen ID, keep each record whose ID is different.
`task.id !== id` means the record's ID does not equal the selected ID. Each button uses its own task's ID, so a label or position change will not select the wrong record.
Two records may have the same text. Their IDs still let you remove only the chosen record. If the ID is absent, every record is kept in a new array.
Complete `without` and connect it to each remove button. Keep the old array unchanged. `filter` makes a new array but shares the kept record objects; it does not copy their contents.

before.question: If the selected ID is absent from the array, what does this filter return?
choices: A new array containing all original elements
before.explanation: Every record has a different ID and passes the predicate. filter creates a new array, while retaining references to its kept objects.

after.question: What does this filter return when the selected ID is absent?
choices: A new array containing all the original items.
after.explanation: Every record has a different ID and is kept. filter still makes a new array.
